easy.def: To poke at something with a short, quick push.
examples: I jab the pencil in the dirt.
She jabbed her finger at the map.
He jabbed at the ice.

more.def: To poke or push something quickly with a pointed thing.
examples: She jabbed her finger at the map to show us the town.
I jabbed a fork into the potato to see if it was done.
He jabbed his stick at the ice to see how thick it was.

easy.def: A quick poke.
examples: He gave me a jab with his finger.
A jab of pain hit her.
The jab was small.

more.def: A quick, short poke or punch.
examples: He gave me a little jab with his elbow to tell me to be quiet.
I felt a sharp jab in my arm from the shot.
A jab of pain hit her when she stood up.

easy.def: To talk fast in a way that is hard to follow.
examples: The kids jabber.
The monkey jabbered.
They jabbered all day.

more.def: To talk quickly and without much sense.
examples: The excited children jabbered all the way home.
The monkeys jabbered in the trees.
She jabbered on and on about her day.

easy.def: A tool for lifting something heavy a little way up.
examples: Dad used a jack to lift the car.
The jack raised the truck.
We need a jack to fix the tire.

more.def: A tool that lifts something heavy a short way off the ground.
examples: She turned the handle of the jack to raise the car.
A jack helps you change a flat tire.
The mechanic put a jack under the truck.

easy.def: A playing card with a picture of a young man on it.
examples: I got a jack.
The jack is in my hand.
She put down the jack.

more.def: A playing card that comes after the ten, with a picture of a young man.
examples: The jack is worth more than a ten in many games.
He held a jack and a queen.
The deck has four jacks, one for each suit.

easy.def: A wild animal like a small dog.
examples: A jackal ran across the field.
The jackal howled at night.
We saw a jackal.

more.def: A wild animal related to dogs that lives in Africa and Asia, and often hunts at night.
examples: A jackal ran across the grassy plain at dusk.
Jackals often hunt in pairs and eat small animals.
The jackal howled at the moon and then trotted away.

easy.def: A small black bird.
examples: A jackdaw sat on the roof.
The jackdaw is black.
I saw a jackdaw.

more.def: A small, black-and-gray bird of the crow family that nests in holes and chimneys.
examples: A jackdaw perched on the chimney.
Jackdaws are clever and often collect shiny things.
A pair of jackdaws nested in the old tower.

easy.def: A short coat.
examples: Put on your jacket.
My jacket is blue.
It is cool, so wear a jacket.

more.def: A short coat that you wear over other clothes.
examples: She zipped up her jacket.
He wore a light jacket on the cool evening.
The jacket has deep pockets.

easy.def: A loud tool that breaks up roads.
examples: The jackhammer is loud.
A jackhammer broke the road.
I heard the jackhammer.

more.def: A heavy, loud tool driven by air that is used to break up hard ground or concrete.
examples: Workers used a jackhammer to break up the old road.
The noise of the jackhammer rattled the windows.
He wore ear protection while using the jackhammer.

easy.def: A very big prize.
examples: She won the jackpot.
The jackpot was big.
We hit the jackpot.

more.def: A very large prize in a game or contest.
examples: She won the jackpot in the school raffle.
The jackpot was a trip to the zoo.
We hit the jackpot when we found a free pizza at the party.

easy.def: A big rabbit with long ears and long back legs.
examples: A jackrabbit ran.
The jackrabbit has long ears.
I saw a jackrabbit.

more.def: A large hare with very long ears and powerful back legs, found in dry places.
examples: A jackrabbit bounded across the desert.
The jackrabbit has huge ears that help it hear.
Jackrabbits can run very fast.

easy.def: A green stone.
examples: The jade is green.
A jade ring.
She wore jade.

more.def: A hard green stone that is used for jewelry and carvings.
examples: The statue was carved from green jade.
She wore a jade ring.
Jade is prized for its color.

easy.def: With rough, pointed edges.
examples: The rock is jagged.
A jagged edge.
The jagged mountains rose.

more.def: Having rough, uneven, sharp edges.
examples: The jagged rocks tore my shoe.
The jagged edge of the torn paper scratched me.
We saw the jagged peaks of the mountains.

easy.def: A big wild cat with spots.
examples: A jaguar lives in the jungle.
The jaguar has spots.
We saw a jaguar at the zoo.

more.def: A large, strong wild cat with a yellow coat covered in dark spots, found in the forests of Central and South America.
examples: A jaguar crept silently through the rain forest at night.
The jaguar's spotted coat helps it hide among the leaves.
Jaguars are strong swimmers and often hunt near rivers.

easy.def: A place where people who did a crime must stay.
examples: The thief went to jail.
The jail is a building.
He was kept in jail.

more.def: A building where people are kept as punishment or while waiting for a trial.
examples: In the story, the thief was sent to jail.
The old jail is now a museum.
A jail has strong doors and locks.

easy.def: An old car in bad shape.
examples: He drove an old jalopy.
The jalopy rattled.
Our jalopy is slow.

more.def: An old, worn-out car that rattles and breaks down.
examples: He drove an old jalopy to the farm.
The jalopy rattled down the road.
Grandpa kept a jalopy in the barn.

easy.def: A sweet, sticky food made from fruit.
examples: I put jam on my toast.
Strawberry jam is sweet.
Grandma made grape jam.

more.def: A sweet, thick spread made by cooking fruit with sugar.
examples: I spread strawberry jam on my toast.
Grandma makes jam from the berries in her garden.
The jar of jam was almost empty.

easy.def: To push into a space or get stuck.
examples: I jam clothes in the bag.
The door jammed.
The copier jammed.

more.def: To push something tightly into a space, or to get stuck and not move.
examples: He jammed the clothes into the small bag.
The drawer jammed and would not open.
The zipper on my coat is jammed.

easy.def: Many cars in a place that cannot move.
examples: There was a traffic jam.
A jam stopped the cars.
We were stuck in a jam.

more.def: A crowd of vehicles or people so close together that they cannot move.
examples: A traffic jam made us late for school.
Cars lined up in a jam on the bridge.
A jam of people blocked the doorway.

easy.def: A big, lively gathering or party.
examples: We went to a jamboree.
The jamboree was fun.
A scout jamboree.

more.def: A large, lively gathering with games and fun, especially of scouts.
examples: The scouts met at a jamboree.
The jamboree had games and music.
We camped at the big jamboree.

easy.def: To make a ringing sound like metal hitting.
examples: The keys jangled.
Her bracelets jangle.
Coins jangled in his pocket.

more.def: To make a harsh ringing sound, like metal pieces hitting together.
examples: Her bracelets jangled as she waved.
Keys jangled in his pocket as he walked.
The bells jangled over the shop door.

easy.def: A person who cleans a building.
examples: The janitor cleans the school.
The janitor has keys.
The janitor mopped the hall.

more.def: A person whose job is to clean and look after a building.
examples: The janitor cleans our school every day.
The janitor fixed the broken light.
The janitor unlocked the doors each morning.

easy.def: The first month of the year.
examples: January is cold.
New Year's Day is in January.
My birthday is in January.

more.def: The first month of the year, after December.
examples: New Year's Day is on the first of January.
It often snows in January.
January has thirty-one days.

easy.def: A glass container with a lid.
examples: The jam is in a jar.
I filled a jar with fireflies.
The jar is full.

more.def: A tall glass or clay container with a wide top and a lid.
examples: The jam is in a glass jar.
She put pennies in a jar.
We caught fireflies in a jar.

easy.def: Special words used by a group.
examples: The doctor used jargon.
Computer jargon.
Jargon is hard.

more.def: Special words or phrases used by people in a particular job or group that others may not understand.
examples: The doctor used medical jargon.
Computer jargon puzzled me.
Avoid jargon when you explain.

easy.def: A sweet-smelling white flower.
examples: The jasmine smells sweet.
I picked jasmine.
The jasmine is white.

more.def: A plant with small, sweet-smelling white or yellow flowers.
examples: The jasmine smelled sweet in the evening.
We drank jasmine tea.
Jasmine climbed up the garden wall.

easy.def: A short, fun trip.
examples: We went on a jaunt.
A jaunt to the park.
It was a happy jaunt.

more.def: A short trip taken for fun.
examples: We went on a jaunt to the beach.
The family took a jaunt to the lake.
It was a cheerful jaunt through the woods.

easy.def: Lively and cheerful.
examples: He wore a jaunty hat.
She has a jaunty walk.
A jaunty tune.

more.def: Cheerful, lively and full of confidence.
examples: He wore his cap at a jaunty angle.
She walked with a jaunty step.
The band played a jaunty tune.

easy.def: A light spear thrown in a sport.
examples: He threw the javelin.
A javelin is long.
The javelin flew far.

more.def: A light spear thrown for distance in track and field.
examples: He threw the javelin far across the field.
The javelin is a light spear.
She won a medal in the javelin throw.

easy.def: The bone that holds your teeth.
examples: The shark has a big jaw.
My jaw hurts.
The dog opened its jaw.

more.def: One of the two bones in your face that hold your teeth and open and close your mouth.
examples: The dog opened its jaws wide.
My jaw was sore after chewing gum.
A shark has strong jaws.

easy.def: The bone of the jaw.
examples: The jawbone is hard.
A fossil jawbone.
The jawbone had teeth.

more.def: The bone that forms the jaw.
examples: The museum had a jawbone from a dinosaur.
The jawbone holds the teeth.
A jawbone was found at the dig.

easy.def: A big, hard candy.
examples: I ate a jawbreaker.
A jawbreaker is hard.
The jawbreaker is round.

more.def: A very hard, round candy that lasts a long time when you suck it.
examples: He sucked on a jawbreaker.
A jawbreaker takes a long time to finish.
The jawbreaker changed color as it dissolved.

easy.def: The bones of the mouth that open and close.
examples: The crocodile opened its jaws.
The shark has strong jaws.
The dog's jaws opened wide.

more.def: The two bones that form the mouth and hold the teeth, which open and close to bite and chew.
examples: The crocodile opened its huge jaws and showed its teeth.
A shark's jaws are strong enough to crush a shell.
The dog's jaws held the ball gently.

easy.def: A noisy bird with blue feathers.
examples: A jay sat in the tree.
The jay is loud.
I saw a blue jay.

more.def: A noisy bird with bright feathers, often blue, that lives in woods.
examples: The blue jay squawked from the top of the oak.
A jay hides acorns in the ground for winter.
Jays often scold other birds with loud calls.

easy.def: To cross a street where you should not.
examples: Do not jaywalk.
He jaywalked.
It is unsafe to jaywalk.

more.def: To cross a street in the wrong place or at the wrong time.
examples: Do not jaywalk; use the crosswalk.
He jaywalked and got a warning.
It is unsafe to jaywalk across a busy street.

easy.def: A kind of music with a lively beat.
examples: I like jazz.
The band plays jazz.
Jazz is fun.

more.def: A type of music that started in the United States, with a lively beat and made-up parts.
examples: The band played jazz on trumpets and saxophones.
I like to dance to jazz.
Jazz musicians often make up their tunes as they play.

easy.def: Bright and lively.
examples: A jazzy hat.
The jazzy tune.
She wore a jazzy shirt.

more.def: Bright, lively and full of style.
examples: She wore a jazzy red hat.
The band played a jazzy tune.
He painted the door a jazzy yellow.
